rule: Use MASAQ Sura_No, Verse_No, Word_No and Segment_No; group segment rows into Quranic word positions before chunking.
review: Check duplicate segments and attached proclitic/enclitic handling.
reason: A word may be split into multiple morphology records; a phrase is not a segment.

rule: Read Phrase markers and phrase-type values from MASAQ; preserve source phrase IDs/types when available.
review: Verify whether marker denotes phrase start, span label or member annotation in each field version.
reason: Source phrase categories do not map one-to-one onto six teaching patterns.

rule: Close candidate spans at the corresponding syntactic boundary using phrase markers, syntactic roles, dependencies and sentence/clause scope.
review: Nested phrases and embedded clauses need human validation.
reason: Do not assume every next marker ends the previous phrase; spans may overlap or nest.

rule: Attach Phrasal_Function to the whole phrase span; keep word-level Syntactic_Role separate.
review: Validate that the function is associated with the full span, not just a head token.
reason: A phrase may function as Khabar, Maf‘ul, Na‘t, Hal, etc. while its member words have internal roles.

rule: Map internal member relations to descriptive, Idafah, prepositional, demonstrative, conjunctive and Badal patterns.
review: Some spans have multiple simultaneous patterns and should support nested labels.
reason: A prepositional phrase can contain an Idafah or adjective phrase.

rule: Clip or split phrase views at Ayah boundaries for teaching, while retaining links to the original cross-Ayah phrase/clause span.
reason: Some source sentence/constituent spans can cross verse boundaries.

rule: Set auto-generated chunks to candidate; publish only after expert or trained reviewer approval.
review: Review ambiguous, elliptical, coordinated and multi-clause cases.
reason: A phrase chunk is a pedagogical analysis, not merely a whitespace split.
